accuracy_findings.claim: The bonus counts the system's mobility from before its percentage bonuses, so a percentage Lex raises the shown mobility but not this bonus. See [[bonus-stacking]].
accuracy_findings.problem: The sentence says this always happens, which contradicts the section 8.1 Bonus stacking verdict. The verdict carries an exception: "Unless a flat conversion runs between them". With a building on this page's own "Buildings that scale with mobility" table (Reflect District, Business Arch), the Mobility bonus counts the raised mobility. Core.Bonus.apply_bonuses refreshes base_state after every :add (bonus.ex:52-56), and :mul bonuses read base_state (bonus.ex:94). Percentage Lex and tradition bonuses on mobility go from sys_mobility to sys_mobility, so they sort at order 29. The Mobility bonus is an order-30 :mul, and every order-30 :add sorts before it. Any flat bonus reading mobility, workforce and similar values therefore refreshes base_state in between. That covers Reflect District and Business Arch, and also Monolith (monument_dome, +ideology per workforce, building-slow.ex:1270), which is not a mobility building. In those systems the Lex does raise the bonus.
accuracy_findings.fix: Keep the default case and name the exception from the verdict, for example: "The bonus usually counts the system's mobility from before its percentage bonuses, so a percentage Lex or tradition raises the shown mobility but not this bonus. Some buildings change that: with a {name:building.<reflect district key>} or {name:building.<business arch key>}, and with some other buildings such as a {name:building.monument_dome}, the bonus counts the raised mobility. See [[bonus-stacking]]." A shorter fix also works: "...but not this bonus, unless the system has a building whose bonus is counted per point of mobility or workforce."

accuracy_findings.problem: The list reads as complete, but those three buildings are not the only cause. Any order-30 flat bonus that reads a system value does the same. Player.extract_bonus sends them to every system, the way it sends traditions (mutators.ex:89-101, player.ex:1191). In a daily with either mutator, every system's Mobility bonus counts the raised mobility. The word 'usually' covers this, so it is not a wrong claim, only an incomplete one.

clarity_findings.claim: The third prose paragraph half-explains the general bonus-stacking mechanism instead of pointing to the page that owns it, and does so in more than one sentence.
clarity_findings.problem: "The bonus usually counts the system's mobility from before its percentage bonuses. So a percentage bonus from a Lex or tradition raises the system's mobility but not this bonus. With a Reflect District, a Business Arch or a Monolith in the system, the bonus counts the raised mobility. See [[bonus-stacking]]." — three sentences restate the general rule for how a resource-converting bonus reads a value relative to percentage bonuses (flat-then-percentage, no compounding, a later flat conversion sees the raised value) before the pointer finally appears. The guide map (docs/help-review/systems/guide-map-rest.md) assigns that formula to system-outputs' bonus-stacking section ("Flat, then percentages of the flat subtotal, no compounding... | system-outputs §bonuses | bonus.ex | Q1") and its own linking-plan row for mobility says only to add "See [[bonus-stacking]]" right after the negative-credit sentence, not to re-derive the mechanism here. This is exactly the pattern rule 4 forbids: "Point instead of half-explaining... Bad: 'The housing factor turns growth negative once population passes housing + 0.75; the housing page explains how it behaves.' Good: 'Above its housing, a system shrinks. See [[housing]].'" It is also a guide-map-topic violation: a topic (bonus stacking mechanics) that the guide map gives to another page is explained here in three sentences, not one.
clarity_findings.fix: Collapse the paragraph to state the mobility-specific outcome in one sentence and link out, e.g. "A percentage bonus (Lex or tradition) does not raise this bonus; a flat conversion building like a {name:building.finance_open} does. See [[bonus-stacking]]." — cutting the restated general rule rather than the mobility-specific fact.
